title: Coastal landforms sequence sheet
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y8 lesson 4 (Coastal landforms sequence sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 4: Which landforms do waves create? (4.3). To understand how erosion and deposition create coastal landforms

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Sediment is deposited into the sea

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: A ridge grows out; its end curves

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: A long ridge of sand or shingle sticking out from the coast

questions.q: Put in order: stack, cave, stump, arch, crack.
questions.model: Start small: a crack. Widen it: a cave. Through the headland: an arch. Roof falls: a stack. Worn down: a stump.

questions.q: Why does soft rock form bays?
questions.a: It erodes faster than hard rock

questions.q: Name a spit in the UK.
Core: Draw a four-stage diagram of a headland eroding into a stack and stump, with labels and processes.
questions.a: Four stages: crack, cave (hydraulic action, abrasion), arch, stack and stump
questions.model: Teacher shows stage 1: headland with a crack at sea level labelled 'hydraulic action widens the crack'.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain how a spit forms (4 to 5 sentences).
questions.a: Longshore drift moves sediment; at a bend in the coast it is deposited into calmer water; a ridge builds out; changing wind curves the end; salt marsh may form behind

questions.q: Stretch: Why are stacks and arches temporary landforms?
questions.a: Erosion continues, so arches collapse and stacks wear down

questions.q: Big question: how does a headland turn into a stack?
questions.a: Erosion widens a crack into a cave, then an arch; the arch collapses leaving a stack
